Wladimir Klitschko, a 39-year-old heavyweight champion, is preparing for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden.  He reflects on his rise to fame, citing his Olympic gold medal win as a turning point in his life and career.  Despite being close to his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age is an advantage, citing his experience and dedication to his training.  Jennings, with a 19-0 record, is focused on countering Klitschko's jab, aiming to exploit its weaknesses through strategic movement and relentless effort.

Derby County lost a 2-1 lead against Watford, drawing 2-2 at home, due to a series of mistakes and a lack of ruthlessness.  Steve McClaren blamed his team for their inability to capitalize on their lead and secure the win, despite having a good performance.  Watford, despite being a man down, fought back to equalize and move within a point of the top two.  Watford's manager Slavisa Jokanovic was proud of his team's resilience and belief in their ability to turn the game around.

Louis van Gaal has opted for a shorter pre-season tour of America for Manchester United, aiming to avoid the fatigue and travel issues that plagued last year's extensive trip. The tour will be approximately 12 days long, ending by August 1st, and will involve playing in the International Champions Cup, a tournament that United won last year. Van Gaal has rejected offers from Asia and Australia, preferring a more manageable schedule and a base location in the west coast. This decision comes after last year's grueling pre-season schedule, which he felt negatively impacted the team's performance.

Despite four penalty appeals in the first half, referee Michael Oliver only awarded one, which was given after Oscar was clearly tripped by David Ospina.  Oliver also cautioned Cesc Fabregas for simulation after a fall, and while Arsenal had an appeal for a penalty on Gary Cahill, Oliver deemed it not a clear foul.  However, replays showed contact on Fabregas, and the booking for diving was harsh.  The article also highlights a missed penalty opportunity for Chelsea when Oscar was clearly fouled by Ospina.

Ryanair has banned passengers from bringing their own alcohol on board flights between Glasgow and Ibiza to ensure safety and comfort. The airline will search all cabin baggage and passengers caught attempting to bring alcohol on board will be denied travel without a refund or compensation. This decision follows a series of incidents involving unruly passengers who consumed alcohol purchased from duty free shops at Glasgow Prestwick Airport. Ryanair claims the ban is in response to customer and airport official consultations and prioritizes the safety and comfort of its passengers and crew.

Chilean pickpockets are the most effective thieves operating in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in the West End. These gangs, often consisting of three to six members, blend in with the crowd and use intelligence-gathering tactics to steal cash, jewelry, and other valuables.  Police are working to combat this organized crime by monitoring CCTV and tracking the movements of these gangs, who often move on to other European cities after a short period in London.  The gangs are often international, with Romanian, Bulgarian, Algerian, and Chilean members.

Lewis Hamilton remains the richest sportsman in Britain with a fortune of £88 million, but Wayne Rooney has overtaken Jenson Button to take second place with a wealth of £72 million.  Rooney's fortune is expected to continue growing as he remains on course to join David Beckham as the only British footballer to surpass £100 million.  Jenson Button is in third place with a fortune of £71 million, while Andy Murray is fourth with £48 million.  British NBA star Luol Deng is in fifth place with a fortune of £40 million.

Alex Gray, a 27-year-old writer, lost 160 pounds over 20 months after years of emotional eating and self-loathing.  He was inspired to make a change after seeing a friend's transformation and realized that he could improve his life by addressing his weight.  Gray's journey involved dietary changes and increased physical activity, leading to a significant improvement in his physical and emotional well-being.  He now feels more confident and comfortable in his own skin, and encourages others struggling with weight to take action and achieve their goals.

Mohammed Nisar, a taxi driver, returned a bag containing £10,000 in cash to passenger Adrian Quinn after realizing he had left it in his taxi. Marco Rubio, seeking the Republican presidential nomination, faces challenges due to his lack of accomplishments and his conservative stances on immigration and Cuba policy, which alienate key demographics.  His past support for immigration reform and his current opposition to Obama's immigration actions have limited his appeal to Latino voters.  Rubio's conservative views on healthcare, government size, and climate change also clash with the preferences of many Hispanic voters.  Despite his youthful energy and Hispanic background, Rubio's lack of bold policy proposals and his perceived lack of leadership make him an unlikely frontrunner.

Kelly Parsons, a 35-year-old dental nurse, has donated 50 eggs to help childless couples conceive, resulting in the birth of twins, twin boys, and a baby boy.  She made the decision to donate after struggling with infertility herself and wanting to help others experience the joy of parenthood.  Parsons has also chosen to allow her egg donor children to contact her daughters when they turn 18, fostering a connection between the families.  Her selfless act has brought happiness to numerous families who were unable to conceive naturally.

A new study reveals that one in five American women are willing to risk their health for cosmetic procedures to achieve an idealized look, despite the potential for long-term damage like hair loss and skin problems.  The study found that women often emulate celebrity beauty trends, but these trends can be harmful and lead to complications like traction alopecia.  While many women believe beauty treatments improve their confidence and appearance, a significant portion remain unaware of the potential risks associated with these procedures.  The study highlights the need for increased education and transparency from beauty salons to inform women about the potential dangers of cosmetic treatments.

Wladimir Klitschko will fight Bryant Jennings on Saturday, aiming to tie Joe Louis's record of 27 heavyweight title defenses.  Despite his age and the challenger's youth and reach advantage, Klitschko remains confident and motivated, stating he will continue fighting as long as he feels healthy and has the drive.  Jennings, however, believes his youth and speed will give him an edge, and he is not intimidated by Klitschko's long reign as champion. Yoshinori Muto, a forward for FC Tokyo, is considering a move to Chelsea this summer, but is weighing his options carefully. Chelsea has reportedly offered around £4 million for Muto, with the intention of loaning him to Vitesse Arnhem next season.  Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho is aware of Muto's potential, but emphasizes the importance of financial considerations and player quality in transfer decisions.  Muto's former manager believes he has the potential to be a success at Stamford Bridge.

Yaya Toure, a Manchester City midfielder, has stated his willingness to leave the club if he doesn't feel challenged or valued. He is open to a move to a new team and is not solely motivated by his high salary. Toure's future at Manchester City is uncertain, as the club is looking to reshape its squad and he has struggled with his form this season. Despite criticism, Toure remains committed to his career and believes he can still perform at a high level.

Andre Cole, a Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of Anthony Curtis, who was stabbed to death by Cole after a dispute over child support payments. Despite claims of mental illness and concerns about the jury's racial makeup, Cole's execution was upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court, which rejected appeals based on mental health and the execution drug's source. Cole's case highlights the issue of racial bias in the justice system, as he was convicted by an all-white jury. This execution marks the third death penalty carried out in Missouri this year.

Russia sent a destroyer, two bombers, and a tanker through the English Channel, prompting the UK to deploy a frigate to monitor them. The Russian aircraft, including long-range Bear bombers capable of carrying nuclear missiles, were escorted away by Typhoon fighter jets after approaching British airspace. Experts believe this may be an attempt by Russia to "snoop" on a NATO war games exercise in Scotland, and the incident highlights rising tensions between the two countries.  The Russian military presence has been increasing, with over 100 Russian aircraft intercepted last year, and the UK is calling for increased defense spending.

Scientists have extracted DNA from a 128,000 to 187,000 year old Neanderthal skeleton nicknamed 'Altamura Man', making it the oldest DNA sample ever recovered from a Neanderthal.  The DNA analysis will provide new insights into the evolution of hominids and the early history of Neanderthals.  Researchers believe that 'Altamura Man' starved to death or died from lack of water, and that his remains were found in a well after a fall. Curtis Stone, a celebrity chef, is committed to feeding his children healthy food and avoids giving them junk food like hot dogs. He believes parents should be responsible for their children's dietary choices and that children will mimic their parents' eating habits. Stone's new cookbook, "Good Food, Good Life," features photos of him cooking and gardening with his wife and son, and he is dedicated to promoting healthy eating habits.  He is also the owner of a successful restaurant in Los Angeles that focuses on one ingredient each month.

Manchester City players are backing Patrick Vieira to replace Manuel Pellegrini if the manager is sacked at the end of the season. Vieira is highly respected by the players and has been praised for his work with the youth team. Despite winning two trophies last season, Pellegrini has failed to secure silverware this campaign and has faced increasing pressure. While Pep Guardiola is the preferred choice, Vieira is emerging as a strong contender if Pellegrini is dismissed.

A herd of buffalo escaped from a farm in upstate New York and crossed the Hudson River, then traveled down the Thruway before being shot dead by law enforcement. The animals had been on the loose for several days, causing traffic disruptions and posing a safety risk to drivers. The owner of the farm admitted he had little hope of capturing the buffalo unharmed and believed tranquilizers and portable corrals would not be effective.  Law enforcement officials decided to shoot the buffalo after experts determined that tranquilizers and portable corrals would not be effective.

Wesley Sneijder, a Galatasaray player, accidentally promoted his knife range on Twitter, on the 15th anniversary of the deaths of two Leeds United fans in Istanbul.  The tweet was met with anger from fans, who pointed out the insensitive timing given the tragic event.  Sneijder deleted the tweet and apologized, acknowledging his lack of awareness about the anniversary.  Leeds fans are planning a minute's silence and tributes to honor the victims.

Eastern European crime gangs are exploiting the EU's free movement rules to operate with impunity, trafficking vulnerable individuals into the UK for forced labor, prostitution, and benefit fraud. The report highlights the exploitation of women, particularly young girls, who are lured to the UK under false pretenses and then forced into servitude or sold for sex. The gangs use sophisticated tactics to control their victims, including seizing their documents and forcing them into debt, while profiting from the UK's welfare system. The report calls for stricter measures to combat this modern slavery trade, including improved passenger name records and increased enforcement of existing laws.

George Osborne refused to rule out further cuts to child benefit if the Conservatives win a second term, suggesting that it could be replaced by Universal Credit. He defended the current welfare system, claiming it has reduced child poverty and inequality, while emphasizing the need for economic security and a growing economy.  The Chancellor also highlighted the potential for further welfare reforms, including restricting child benefit to two children, which could save money and encourage responsible family planning.  However, critics argue that these cuts disproportionately affect middle-income families and could further exacerbate inequality.

The Australian Vaccination Skeptics Network (AVN) sparked controversy by posting an image comparing mandatory vaccinations to rape on their Facebook page. The post, which has since been removed, drew widespread criticism for its insensitive and inappropriate comparison. The AVN, which has a history of using the rape metaphor to oppose vaccinations, has faced scrutiny for its misleading information and potential harm to public health.  The group has been criticized for its lack of accuracy and for potentially endangering public health.

The stadium, set to host matches up to the quarter-finals in 2022, will have a capacity of 21,000 after the World Cup and will be built on the site of a previous stadium. Liverpool secured a 1-0 victory over Blackburn Rovers in the FA Cup, advancing to the semi-finals.  Philippe Coutinho scored the winning goal and had a dominant performance, while Jordan Henderson, who had a newborn daughter the night before, delivered a captain's performance despite lack of sleep.  The win comes after a review meeting with the players, which Brendan Rodgers believes helped them bounce back from a recent loss.  Liverpool will now face Aston Villa in the semi-finals at Wembley.

A group of individuals, known as the "tattoo terrorists," were convicted for the brutal assault of a 53-year-old man, Greg Valecce. The assault, which took place in a Philadelphia basement, involved physical violence, torture, and the application of offensive tattoos. The ringleader, Corry Campbell, received a 20-year sentence, while his accomplices Sandra Ng and Carl Halin received 23 months and 20 years respectively. The incident was motivated by Campbell's belief that Valecce had harmed his cat and resulted in severe injuries for the victim.

An 11-year-old autistic boy drew a highly accurate world map from memory in a New York classroom, showcasing his exceptional memory and visual skills. The boy, who is the son of a professor, drew the map on a whiteboard while kneeling on a chair, demonstrating impressive detail and accuracy, including political borders and tiny coastal islands. The image of the boy's accomplishment has gone viral on Reddit, sparking admiration and highlighting the diverse abilities within the autistic community.  While some individuals with autism may face memory challenges, others possess unique strengths, such as exceptional memory and visual skills.

Stephen Adly Guirgis' play "Between Riverside and Crazy" won the Pulitzer for drama, while Elizabeth Kolbert's "The Sixth Extinction" won for general nonfiction.  Other Pulitzer winners in the arts and letters categories include works in history, biography, music, and poetry.  The Pulitzer Prizes are highly prestigious awards administered by Columbia University.

Collette Dinnigan, the renowned fashion designer, is selling her Paddington home after purchasing a waterfront property in Watsons Bay. The four-bedroom 19th century sandstone house, renovated to blend contemporary and period style, is expected to sell for $6 million. Dinnigan, who has a history of selling her properties, recently sold her Palm Beach home for $3.2 million and is now focusing on her family.  The sale of the Paddington home follows her purchase of a lavish waterfront property in Watsons Bay.

A Texas A&M professor, Irwin Horwitz, decided to fail his entire strategic management class after accusing students of cheating, disruptive behavior, and disrespect. He claimed the students lacked the honor and maturity to meet the course standards and that he was disgusted by their behavior. The university has stated that Horwitz's decision will not stand and that each student will be evaluated individually by the department head.  Horwitz, who has taught for 20 years, will not teach the class again.

Indonesian officials have ordered the preparation for the executions of Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran, the Bali Nine ringleaders, with the Australian Embassy summoned to Nusakambangan Island.  The executions are expected to take place within days, with the Indonesian government giving 72 hours' notice to the prisoners and their families.  President Joko Widodo has confirmed the executions will happen after the conclusion of all legal appeals, and only one legal matter remains outstanding.  Chan and Sukumaran's lawyers had hoped for another legal challenge, but the Attorney-General has stated that a Constitutional Court challenge will not be considered.

Porto, despite holding a 3-1 lead from the first leg, will need to perform at their best to overcome Bayern Munich in their Champions League quarter-final.  Bayern is missing key players like Robben, Alaba, and Ribery, but still poses a significant threat, with Schweinsteiger returning to training but doubtful to start. Porto will be without suspended players Danilo and Alex Sandro, but have key players like Jackson Martinez and Ricardo Quaresma in good form.  Coach Julen Lopetegui believes a strong performance is crucial to advance, despite the challenge of facing one of the greatest teams in history.

Twitter has launched a new feature called "Highlights" to help users manage their feed by providing a twice-daily summary of popular tweets from people they follow.  Highlights are available on Android devices and are powered by an algorithm that considers trending topics, popular accounts, and connections.  This feature is being rolled out first in English for Android users and Twitter is also taking steps to combat abuse on the platform, including temporarily locking abusive accounts and automatically removing abusive content.  Twitter is also testing a feature to identify and remove suspected abusive tweets from users' notifications.

Len Barnes, a 75-year-old man suffering from a life-threatening bowel infection, was cured after undergoing a faecal transplant using his daughter's stool. The procedure, which involves introducing healthy bacteria from a donor's stool into the patient's gut, was successful in restoring balance to his gut bacteria and eliminating the infection.  The procedure, which was deemed safe enough for NHS use, has been shown to be effective in treating Clostridium difficile infections, with a high cure rate and minimal recurrence.  The success of faecal transplants highlights the potential of this innovative treatment for various gut-related conditions.

Chelsea are in early talks with Belgian club Royal Mouscron-Peruwelz to potentially form a partnership. This comes after Lille, Mouscron's previous partner, ended their agreement, creating an opportunity for Chelsea. Mouscron is currently in the Belgian Pro League, and Chelsea are exploring partnerships across Europe to develop their squad.  This follows Chelsea's existing agreement with Vitesse Arnhem in Holland.

Manchester United will wear Nike kit during their upcoming US tour despite their new £750 million deal with Adidas. This is because there is no buy-out clause in their existing Nike contract, which runs until the end of July. The tour will be shorter than last year, likely confined to the west coast, and will end on August 1st, potentially allowing fans to see the new Adidas kit in the following season.  Louis van Gaal, the manager, has been instrumental in limiting the tour to 12 days to avoid the negative effects of last year's extensive tour.

Portsmouth have sacked manager Andy Awford following a 3-1 defeat to Morecambe, leaving them with a significant gap to the top seven in League Two. Awford's departure comes after a year in charge, during which he won 20 of his 55 matches. Assistant manager Gary Waddock will now take caretaker charge of the team. Portsmouth expressed gratitude for Awford's service and highlighted his crucial role in keeping the club in the Football League in 2014.

A teenage boy, Jaidyn, suffered serious injuries including a broken jaw and fractured cheekbone after being assaulted at an Adelaide train station. The attack occurred after a dispute over money owed for a hot dog, and the attackers demanded $15 from Jaidyn, who only had $5.  Jaidyn's mother, Kat Lee, shared images of his injuries on Facebook, urging witnesses to come forward. Police are investigating the incident, but no arrests have been made.

Justine Jones, a mother with a sensitive immune system, developed severe welts and sores after drinking a bottle of Tesco wine that reeked of bleach. The family found the wine contaminated despite the bottle being sealed and showed no signs of tampering.  Tesco initially responded with a superficial investigation and a small monetary compensation, which Mrs. Jones deemed inadequate.  The family is demanding a thorough investigation and accountability from Tesco for the incident.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA Men's Basketball Final Four, 71-64, to advance to the championship game.  Frank Kaminsky led Wisconsin with 20 points and 11 rebounds, while Kentucky's 38-0 record came to an end. Duke, meanwhile, dominated Michigan State 81-61, led by Jahlil Okafor and Justise Winslow. A computer outage affecting 8,000 Starbucks stores in the US and Canada caused disruptions, leading to free drinks being given away by baristas. The outage, which began in the early evening and was caused by a system refresh failure, has now been resolved and stores are expected to reopen normally. While some locations offered free drinks, others closed to avoid giving away free products. Despite the outage, Starbucks reported record quarterly earnings earlier in the week, with net revenues of $4.6 billion.

A devastating 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Nepal, causing avalanches at Everest and nearby peaks, resulting in at least 17 confirmed deaths and many more injured.  The earthquake has disrupted the climbing season, with some climbers trapped above the icefall and communication hampered.  While some climbers have been evacuated, others remain stranded, and the death toll is expected to rise as rescue efforts continue.  Despite the tragedy, many climbers are determined to return to Everest, drawn by its allure and the challenge it presents.

Former Utah high school English teacher Brianne Altice pleaded guilty to three counts of forcible sexual abuse involving three male students, avoiding a trial. Altice, who was in a position of special trust, had sexual relationships with the boys, who were all minors at the time. She faces up to 45 years in prison when sentenced next month. The school district is facing lawsuits alleging negligence in failing to fire Altice despite knowing about her inappropriate behavior.

This style reflects his gritty and resilient playing style, and he has maintained it throughout his career, even after joining West Brom. The victory moved West Brom to 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their safety in the Premier League.

Police officers in New Jersey responded to a report of an erratic driver and found a flipped convertible with a woman trapped inside.  The officers quickly cut the seatbelt and dragged the unconscious woman to safety, but the car exploded shortly after.  The woman, Dawn Milosky, survived the crash and was charged with several offenses, including driving under the influence. The officers' quick action and bravery are highlighted in the video footage released by the police department.

Despite Abbott's support, McGregor expressed sadness that he is not a supporter of same-sex marriage. Marco Rubio has announced his candidacy for the Republican presidential nomination, but his chances are hindered by his lack of appeal to Latino voters, whom he has alienated with his stance on immigration reform and Cuba relations. His retreat on immigration reform and his opposition to President Obama's Deferred Action program and executive action on immigration have made him unpopular among Hispanics. Rubio's Cuba policy is also out of touch with the majority of Americans and Cuban-Americans, who support better relations with the communist country. His lack of bold policy proposals and significant accomplishments in the Senate make it difficult for him to stand out as a candidate.

Kelly Parsons, a 35-year-old dental nurse from London, has donated 50 eggs to help childless couples conceive, resulting in three successful pregnancies, including twins and a baby boy. She has been donating eggs since 2011, after struggling with infertility for eight years and experiencing three miscarriages. Kelly's eggs have been frozen for future use, and she has chosen to inform her 11-year-old daughter that she has brothers and sisters, who will be able to contact her when they turn 18. One in five American women are willing to undergo beauty treatments despite the risks to their health, with 7% experiencing allergic reactions and 4% continuing with treatments despite knowing they may cause permanent damage. The survey found that 53% of women get inspiration for hairstyles from celebrities like Jennifer Aniston and Sandra Bullock, but warns that emulating these looks can lead to long-term problems. Despite the dangers, most women believe beauty treatments boost their confidence and make them feel better about themselves. The study highlights the need for education and transparency in the beauty industry, with 56% of respondents wanting more information on the side effects of their treatments

Wladimir Klitschko will fight American Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden, aiming to match Joe Louis's record of 27 heavyweight title fights. The 39-year-old Ukrainian has dominated the division for nearly a decade and has 17 consecutive successful title defenses. Jennings, 30, believes his youth and speed will give him an edge against the experienced champion, while Klitschko is confident in his technical skills and plans to continue his reign.

FC Tokyo forward Yoshinori Muto is considering a move to Chelsea this summer, with the club reportedly offering £4million for the 22-year-old Japan international. Muto wants to join a club where he can play regularly and develop his skills, and is weighing up the offer against other options. Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho has acknowledged the club's interest in Muto, but has emphasized the importance of financial considerations in the transfer process. Muto is taking his time to consider the offer and is looking for a team that suits him.

Yaya Toure has hinted that he is open to leaving Manchester City this summer, citing a desire for new challenges and a feeling that he no longer belongs at the club. The 31-year-old midfielder has struggled to hit top form this season, and City are likely to try and sell him in the summer. Toure's former manager Roberto Mancini is now in charge at Inter Milan and is reportedly interested in reuniting with the player. Toure has stated that he will not stay at City just for the money, and is willing to leave if a new challenge is not presented to him.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri for killing a man, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments 16 years ago. Cole was convicted by an all-white jury and had several appeals denied by the US Supreme Court, including one claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution. Cole's execution was carried out despite concerns about the fairness of his trial, with advocates arguing that he was denied a fair trial due to the all-white jury. Cole was pronounced dead at 10:24pm on Tuesday, marking the third execution in Missouri this year.

A Russian warship and two bombers strayed close to UK territory, prompting a response from the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force. The incident is believed to be an attempt to "snoop" on a NATO war games exercise taking place in Scotland, with Russian President Vladimir Putin possibly using the opportunity to test UK reaction times. The Russian aircraft were intercepted by Typhoon fighter jets, and the incident is the latest in a long line of apparent tests by Moscow as tensions between Britain and Russia rise. The incident has raised concerns about Russia's intentions and the need for increased defence spending to counter a "resurgent" Russia.

Scientists in Italy have extracted DNA from the 128,000 to 187,000-year-old "Altamura Man" skeleton, which is the oldest ever DNA sample from a Neanderthal. The DNA was extracted from a tiny part of the shoulder bone, which was analyzed in the lab over a six-year period. The team plans to sequence the DNA to reveal new details about the evolution of our ancient ancestors and potentially shed light on why Neanderthals went extinct. The DNA may also hold clues about the evolution of modern humans and the impact of interbreeding with Neanderthals on our health.

Curtis Stone, a celebrity chef, is adamant that his children should eat healthy food and has never allowed them to eat hot dogs due to their high nitrate content. He believes that parents are responsible for shaping their children's eating habits and that kids will adopt whatever they are exposed to. Stone's new cookbook, Good Food, Good Life, features photos of him cooking and gardening with his wife and son, and he has dedicated it to his eldest son. Stone's restaurant, Maude, has received critical acclaim and has been named one of the best new restaurants in LA.

Manchester City players have expressed support for Patrick Vieira to replace Manuel Pellegrini as manager, following a disappointing campaign. Vieira is highly respected among the players and has done well with the club's youth team. However, Pep Guardiola remains the club's top choice, although he has indicated he will listen to offers from English clubs in the summer. If Guardiola is not available, Vieira is seen as a strong contender to replace Pellegrini, who is under pressure following a 4-2 defeat to Manchester United.

A herd of 15 buffalo escaped from a farm in upstate New York and swam across the Hudson River, prompting law enforcement to shoot and kill the animals. The buffalo then ran down the Thruway, a toll road that connects major cities in the state, before being shot by three men hired by the farm. The decision to shoot the animals was made after experts deemed tranquilizers ineffective and portable corrals unable to hold them. The buffalo were last seen heading into woods near the Massachusetts Turnpike.

Wesley Sneijder, a Galatasaray striker, launched his knife range on the 15th anniversary of two Leeds United supporters being stabbed to death in Istanbul in 2000. Sneijder tweeted an advertisement for his knife set, which was met with outrage from Leeds fans who were still grieving the loss of Kevin Speight and Christopher Loftus. Sneijder later deleted the tweet and apologized, saying he was unaware of the anniversary and did not mean to offend. A minute's silence will be held before a Championship match between Leeds and Blackburn Rovers to mark the anniversary.

Chancellor George Osborne has refused to rule out further cuts to child benefit if the Conservatives win a second term, despite previously cutting the benefit for families with one parent earning £50,000. The Coalition has already saved £21 billion in this Parliament, and Osborne has hinted that further reforms to welfare could be on the cards. The Institute for Fiscal Studies has suggested that increasing Universal Credit for some families could save £4.8 billion a year, but Osborne has ruled out replacing child benefit with Universal Credit. The Conservatives aim to cut £12 billion from the welfare bill, with child benefit potentially being one of the areas targeted.

The Australian Vaccination Skeptics Network posted a social media image comparing compulsory vaccination to rape, sparking widespread outrage and condemnation. The image was posted in response to new vaccination laws, but the group's president denied any affiliation with the post. The Australian Vaccination Skeptics Network has a history of using inflammatory language to oppose vaccinations, and has been stripped of its registered charity status and faced investigations into its fundraising activities. The group's actions have been widely criticized as irresponsible and triggering for survivors of sexual assault.

Qatar has unveiled the design for its fifth World Cup stadium, the 40,000-seater Al Rayyan Stadium, which features a sand dune-inspired design and air conditioning for player and fan comfort. The stadium is expected to host matches up to the quarter-final stage of the 2022 World Cup and will be completed in early 2019. The stadium's design includes seven patterns representing different aspects of Qatari culture, and it will be built near other sports facilities and amenities. The stadium's capacity will be reduced to 21,000 seats after the World Cup.

Liverpool advanced to the FA Cup semi-finals with a 1-0 win over Blackburn Rovers, thanks to Philippe Coutinho's goal and a crucial assist from captain Jordan Henderson. Henderson, who had not slept the night before due to the birth of his second daughter, put in a "real captain's performance" despite being exhausted. An 11-year-old boy with autism drew a highly accurate world map from scratch, including details such as political borders and tiny coastal islands, in a classroom setting. The boy, who is the son of a professor, was invited to the class and drew the map on a whiteboard while kneeling on a chair. The map was so detailed that it included labels for major countries and even small islands. The boy's exceptional memory and visual skills are a testament to the diversity of abilities among individuals with autism.

Anthony Doerr's novel "All the Light We Cannot See" won the Pulitzer Prize for fiction, his second novel and fourth work of fiction. The novel, set during World War II, had received rave reviews upon its release last spring. Doerr's work was also a finalist for the National Book Award, and he is the second author to win the Pulitzer Prize for fiction in 2015, following Stephen Adly Guirgis for his play "Between Riverside and Crazy". The Pulitzer Prizes are administered by Columbia University and recognize excellence in journalism and literature.

Collette Dinnigan, a renowned fashion designer, has listed her luxurious Paddington home on the market for $6 million after purchasing a new waterfront home in Watsons Bay for $6.5 million. The couple had a history of domestic violence, and the judge considered this when handing down the sentence. Robarge's daughter, Ciera, expressed her mother's love and said she did not deserve to die. Robarge has served nearly two years behind bars and could be eligible for parole in about 28 years.

Indonesian officials have sent letters to the prosecutors of 10 death row prisoners, including Australians Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran, ordering preparations for their executions. The letters indicate that the executions could take place as early as Monday or Tuesday, with the Australian Embassy being summoned to Nusakambangan Island on Saturday. The Indonesian Attorney-General's spokesman has confirmed that only one legal matter remains outstanding, which is expected to be finalized within days. The executions will be carried out by firing squad, with Sukumaran and Chan facing the same fate.

Porto will face a tough challenge against Bayern Munich in the Champions League quarter-final, despite holding a 3-1 first leg advantage. Bayern, who are missing several key players, are still considered a lethal team and will be looking to overturn the deficit. Porto manager Julen Lopetegui believes his team will need to produce a great performance to progress, but acknowledges it will be a difficult task. The match is set to be a highly competitive and intense encounter.

Twitter has launched a new feature called "Highlights" that provides a twice-daily summary of the best tweets for users, delivered via rich push notifications. The feature is currently available in English for Android users and aims to help users sift through the large number of tweets on their feed each day. Highlights takes into account popular accounts, trending topics, and user interactions to curate a personalized feed. The feature is part of Twitter's efforts to boost engagement and combat abuse on the platform.

A 57-year-old man, Len Barnes, was cured of a severe bowel infection caused by Clostridium difficile after undergoing a faecal transplant. The procedure involved mixing his daughter's healthy stools with his own and transplanting the solution into his gut via an endoscope. The faecal transplant was successful in balancing the bacteria in his gut and eliminating the infection, with Len losing three stone and experiencing significant weight loss and pain. The procedure has been deemed safe and effective by the NHS and has been recognized as a treatment option for C-diff infections by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence.

Chelsea are in early discussions with Belgian club Royal Mouscron-Peruwelz over a possible partnership, following the end of their existing deal with Lille. Mouscron, currently 13th in the Pro League, are looking to link up with another Belgian club, Ostend, leaving room for a new deal with Chelsea. This would be Chelsea's second partnership in the Eredivisie, following their existing agreement with Vitesse Arnhem. The partnership would help develop Chelsea's squad, with players including Josh McEachran and Bertrand Traore currently on loan at Vitesse.

Manchester United will wear Nike kit during their summer US tour, despite signing a world-record deal with adidas. The club's existing deal with Nike runs until the end of July, and there is no buy-out clause that would allow them to exit the agreement early. The 12-day tour, which will be confined to the west coast, will not allow for the new adidas kit to be showcased. The tour will take place before August 1, when the new kit is expected to be available.

Portsmouth have sacked manager Andy Awford following a 3-1 defeat to Morecambe, which left the team with an 11-point gap to the top seven with four games left. Awford, 42, had been in charge for just over a year and won 20 of 55 matches. He will be replaced by assistant manager Gary Waddock, who will take caretaker charge of the team ahead of the clash with Stevenage. Awford's departure comes after a significant contribution to the club's safety from relegation in 2014.

A teenage boy was assaulted at an Adelaide train station on Saturday night after a dispute over a hot dog, resulting in serious injuries including a broken jaw and fractured cheekbone. His mother, Kat Lee, has released images of his injuries and appealed for witnesses to come forward, which has gone viral on Facebook. The incident occurred after the boy's attackers, including four teenagers and an adult, demanded payment for a hot dog, despite the boy only owing $5. Police are investigating the matter, but no arrests have been made.

A mother of two, Justine Jones, claimed that a bottle of Tesco Finest Garnacha wine she opened to celebrate her daughter's 18th birthday left her face covered in angry red welts and huge sores. The bottle was found to contain a clear liquid with a strong bleach-like smell, despite being sealed and showing no signs of tampering. Justine suffers from a rare condition that makes her immune system sensitive to certain chemicals, making her particularly vulnerable to the effects of the wine. Tesco has apologized for its handling of the investigation and promised to look into the matter to prevent similar incidents in the future.

The Kentucky Wildcats lost to the Wisconsin Badgers 71-64 in the NCAA men's basketball Final Four, ending their bid for a perfect season. Wisconsin rallied from a 60-56 deficit with 6:39 left in the game, going on an 8-0 run to regain the lead and never relinquishing it. The Badgers will face Duke in the title game, while Duke defeated Michigan State 81-61 in the first contest of the night. Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky led the team with 20 points and 11 rebounds, while Duke's Jahlil Okafor had 18 points.

Starbucks announced a computer outage that affected 8,000 stores in the US and Canada, prompting baristas to give away free drinks to customers. The outage, which began in the late afternoon on the West Coast and early evening on the East Coast, was caused by a failure during a daily system refresh. The company has since resolved the issue and stores are expected to reopen on Saturday. The outage resulted in some locations closing early to avoid giving away free products, but many customers took advantage of the impromptu giveaway.

A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Nepal, causing widespread devastation and triggering avalanches on Mount Everest, killing at least 17 people, including 13 mountaineers from a base camp. Many more are feared dead, with some reports suggesting the death toll could be as high as 200. Several foreign companies that bring climbers to Everest reported fatalities, including an American who died in the avalanche and a base camp medic who was killed. The Indian Army's Everest Expedition evacuated the bodies of the deceased, while rescue efforts are ongoing, with many survivors sharing harrowing accounts of their experiences on social media.

Former Utah high school teacher Brianne Altice, 35, pleaded guilty to three counts of forcible sexual abuse involving three male students, who were 16 and 17 years old at the time. She accepted a plea deal that dropped 11 other counts, including several first-degree felonies, in exchange for a possible 45-year prison sentence. School officials were aware of Altice's inappropriate behavior, but failed to take action, and several students have filed lawsuits against the Davis County School District alleging negligence. Pep Guardiola craved stability and chose clubs based on such assurances, which is why he opted to join Bayern Munich instead of Chelsea in 2012. Chelsea's owner Roman Abramovich had recruited players in anticipation of Guardiola's arrival, but he was spooked by Abramovich's habit of hiring and firing managers. Manchester City are now facing a similar situation, with Manuel Pellegrini's position under threat, and are considering appointing Patrick Vieira as interim manager until Guardiola becomes available, which is expected to be in 2016.

Tony Pulis led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, with goals from James Morrison and Craig Gardner. Pulis, known for his distinctive pre-match attire, claimed he would never change his routine, which includes wearing a cap, track suit, and trainers. The win moved West Brom to 36 points, guaranteeing their safety in the Premier League. Pulis has transformed the team since taking over, much like he did at Crystal Palace last season.

A 45-year-old woman, Dawn Milosky, was rescued by two police officers after her car crashed and caught fire on a New Jersey roadway. The officers, Mark Ehrenburg and Ricky Ferriola, freed the unconscious driver from her seatbelt and provided CPR before she was airlifted to a hospital, where she survived. The driver was later charged with multiple offenses, including driving while intoxicated. The police released a dashcam video of the rescue, which showed the officers' bravery and quick thinking in saving the woman's life.

Cate McGregor, a former Australian Army officer and current Group Captain in the Royal Australian Air Force, was publicly backed by Prime Minister Tony Abbott after she transitioned from a man to a woman. However, when she shared her chapter about her transformation in her book, Abbott responded with a conciliatory message, saying "it was okay". McGregor believes Abbott's support was genuine and that he was unfairly vilified by some for his stance on same-sex marriage. She has praised Abbott's willingness to risk party divisions to support her.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has defended his decision to drop out of signing Eden Hazard in 2012, citing financial constraints as the reason. Hazard joined Chelsea for £32million, a deal that Wenger believed Arsenal could not afford. Despite this, Wenger acknowledges that Hazard has improved significantly and is now a strong contender for the Player of the Year award. Wenger believes that Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez will also give Hazard a run for his money in the voting.

Two hitmen, Christopher Annan and Tyrone Wright, have been jailed for a total of 44 years for their roles in a gun attack on Tottenham Turks gang member Inan Eren in 2012. English clubs face significant financial and talent disparities compared to their French opponents, making a breakthrough unlikely. However, Bath and Saracens are considered the most likely English teams to progress to the next round.

Arsenal will wear their yellow and blue away strip for the FA Cup final against Aston Villa on May 30, a color combination that has brought them success in the past, including three cup final wins in five appearances. Mark Doggett, a 30-year-old businessman from Wolverhampton, has trained his two dogs, Meg and Jess, to detect dry rot in old houses using their exceptional sense of smell. Oldham Athletic have signed 16-year-old Ronaldo Brown, a winger with explosive pace, after he was released by Liverpool. Brown is the latest addition to Oldham's squad, with the club looking to make a statement with a marquee signing to mark the opening of a new stand. The signing is seen as a promising move for the League One club, who have remained in the division for 18 years.

Manny Pacquiao will wear the world's most expensive shorts, valued at $2.25m, in his upcoming fight against Floyd Mayweather on May 2. The fight will also feature sponsorship logos from six companies on Pacquiao's trunks, with the identity of the companies on his shorts yet to be revealed. The fight is expected to be one of the most lucrative in boxing history.

Two victims of the Boston Marathon bombing, Jessica Kensky and Patrick Downes, have spoken out against the death penalty for Dzhokar Tsarnaev, urging him to be sentenced to life in prison without parole instead. The couple, who lost limbs in the 2013 attack, say that seeking the death penalty would prolong their pain and reliving the traumatic event. The jury will decide whether to sentence Tsarnaev to death or life in prison without parole.

Vera Baird, the Police and Crime Commissioner for Northumbria, has been accused of a conflict of interest after awarding £500,000 of public money to a charity she runs alongside the force's chief, Sue Sim. The charity, Victims First Northumbria, supports crime victims in her area and is also funded by the Ministry of Justice. The decision has sparked a Ministry of Justice investigation and criticism from Labour chairman Keith Vaz, who says it is "inappropriate" for a PCC to set up a charity with a personal interest. The investigation will determine whether any conflict of interest rules were broken.

John Higgins and Graeme Dott led the Scottish charge at the Betfred World Championship, with Higgins defeating Robert Milkins 10-5 in the first round. Higgins, 39, looked to be in form, firing breaks of 77, 75, and 106, and is now eyeing a potential fifth world title. He had previously expressed doubts about his ability to win again, but his victory over Milkins has given him a boost. Higgins is now in contention, with a number of top players ahead of him in terms of titles won.

A four-year-old boy, Jayden Wingler, was interviewed by Fox News about a theme park accident that left him with severe burns on his legs. Despite having bandaged wounds, Jayden gave a vivid and animated account of the incident, using arm actions and facial expressions to convey his emotions. The interview was watched thousands of times and received positive comments from viewers, with many praising Jayden's personality and charisma. Jayden and his brother were injured in a bumper boat ride accident at Castles N' Coasters amusement park in Phoenix, Arizona.

Lillian Bustle, a burlesque performer, is using her platform to challenge negative perceptions of the word "fat" and promote body positivity. She argues that the word "fat" is just another self-descriptor and doesn't have to be used as an insult, and that beauty comes in all shapes and sizes. Bustle's TED talk has been well-received, with many viewers praising her message and sharing their own positive body image experiences. The talk has also sparked a wider conversation about body diversity and size discrimination, with some statistics showing a significant increase in workplace discrimination against larger individuals.

Gemma Collins, a 34-year-old star of The Only Way Is Essex, has launched a new plus-size fashion range for Evans, featuring seven new curve-flattering tops and dresses. The collection is designed to inspire voluptuous women to feel more confident and embracing their curves. Collins, who has expanded her popular range, aims to show that plus-size fashion is evolving and becoming more stylish, and that confidence is key to feeling good. The collection is stocked in 16 Evans stores nationwide and on their website, and Collins plans to use her platform to promote body positivity and self-acceptance.

Luke Rockhold is set to face Lyoto Machida in a middleweight bout, seeking his fourth consecutive victory since losing to Vitor Belfort two years ago. Rockhold plans to "be the bull" and dominate Machida, using his speed and agility to outmaneuver the Japanese fighter. Machida, meanwhile, is confident he can upset Rockhold and earn a title shot, citing his own strategy and technique as key to his success. The two fighters have mutual respect for each other, but Rockhold is determined to prove himself as the better fighter.

Reports emerged that Mike Ashley, owner of Newcastle United, has gained control of Rangers' trademarks, including the "Ready" badge and mascot Broxi Bear, following a £5m loan to the club in January. The club has promised to investigate the claims, with a spokesman stating that a review of contractual documentation is underway. The club's new regime, led by Dave King, has vowed to look into the matter urgently.

Manchester United midfielder Marouane Fellaini was the subject of a mix-up involving Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho prior to their match on April 18. Mourinho had prepared his team to deal with Fellaini, but was told by a hotel doorman that the Belgian was not playing, as he was actually there to get tickets for the game. Fellaini was substituted at half-time against Everton on Sunday, and spent Tuesday relaxing with his twin brother Mansour. Fellaini did play at Stamford Bridge earlier this month, but was limited to midfield against Chelsea.

Andy Murray lost his seventh consecutive match to Novak Djokovic in the Miami Open final, 7-6 4-6 6-0. A study on ancient tooth plaque has revealed that a 35-40 year old woman, known as the Red Lady of El Mirón, ate mushrooms as part of her diet around 18,700 years ago. The remains of several mushroom species, including bolete and gilled mushrooms, were found trapped in her hardened dental plaque. The discovery provides the oldest evidence yet of human mushroom consumption and sheds new light on the mysterious Red Lady's diet, which also included plant pollen, seeds, and animal products. The findings suggest that the Red Lady's diet was varied and supplemented animal staples with plant-like foods.

Police have discovered a body believed to be 36-year-old Samantha Fleming, a young Indiana woman who was reported missing with her newborn daughter Serenity, in a home in Gary, Indiana. The infant was found unharmed and will be returned to relatives. Police believe Fleming was lured to the home by a woman claiming to be from the Indiana Department of Child Services, who was later identified as a person of interest in the case. The woman, who is believed to be the alleged kidnapper's sister, had been planning the scheme, which included setting up a nursery and preparing for a newborn baby.

Rubio's Cuba policy is also at odds with the majority of Americans and Cuban-Americans, who support better relations with the country. Kelly Parsons, a 35-year-old dental nurse from London, has donated 50 eggs to help childless couples conceive, resulting in three successful pregnancies, including twins and a baby boy. She underwent the painful donation procedure three times, using medications to stop her period and stimulate her ovaries. Kelly's eggs have been used by two couples to have twins and another woman to give birth to a boy, and she has frozen some of her eggs for future use. Kelly's decision to donate her eggs was motivated by her own struggles with infertility and her desire to help others who are unable to conceive naturally.

One in five American women are willing to undergo beauty treatments despite the risks to their health, with 7% experiencing allergic reactions and 4% continuing with treatments despite knowing they may cause permanent damage. Despite the dangers, most women believe beauty treatments boost their confidence and make them feel better about themselves. The study highlights the need for education and transparency in the beauty industry to inform women about the potential risks of cosmetic treatments.

Jennings, a 30-year-old challenger from Philadelphia, believes his youth and speed will give him an edge against the experienced Klitschko. A win for Klitschko would also move him within one of Larry Holmes's record 19 consecutive title defenses.

Marco Rubio has announced his candidacy for the Republican presidential nomination, but faces significant challenges in winning over Latino voters due to his stance on immigration reform and Cuba relations. His retreat on immigration reform and opposition to President Obama's executive action on immigration have alienated many Latino voters. Rubio's Cuba policy is also at odds with the majority of Americans and Cuban-Americans, who support better relations with the country. His lack of bold policy proposals and significant accomplishments in the Senate make it difficult for him to differentiate himself from other Republican candidates.

Kelly Parsons, a 35-year-old dental nurse from London, has donated 50 eggs to help childless couples conceive, resulting in three successful pregnancies, including twins and a baby boy. She underwent the painful donation procedure three times, using drugs to stop her period and stimulate her ovaries. Kelly's eggs have been used by two couples to have twins and another woman to give birth to a boy, and she has frozen some of her eggs for future use. Kelly's decision to donate her eggs was motivated by her own struggles with infertility and her desire to help others who are unable to conceive naturally.

One in five American women are willing to undergo beauty treatments despite the risks to their health, with 7% experiencing allergic reactions and 4% continuing with treatments despite knowing they may cause permanent damage. The survey found that 53% of women cite celebrity hairstyles as inspiration, but many of these looks can lead to long-term problems such as hair loss and skin swelling. Despite the dangers, most women believe beauty treatments boost their confidence and make them feel better about themselves. The study highlights the need for education and transparency in the beauty industry to inform women about the potential risks of cosmetic treatments.

Wladimir Klitschko will fight Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden, aiming to match Joe Louis's record of 27 heavyweight title fights. The 39-year-old Ukrainian has dominated the division for nearly a decade and has no plans to retire, with 17 successful title defenses under his belt. Jennings, a 30-year-old challenger from Philadelphia, believes his youth and speed will give him an edge against the experienced Klitschko. A win for Klitschko would also move him within one of Larry Holmes's record 19 consecutive title defenses.

FC Tokyo forward Yoshinori Muto is considering a move to Chelsea this summer, with the Premier League club believed to have made an offer of around £4million. Muto wants to join a club where he can play regularly and develop his skills, and is weighing up the opportunity to join Chelsea, who have a strong commercial interest in signing him. Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho has admitted to being aware of Muto, but has not commented on the potential transfer. Muto's current club, FC Tokyo, are keen to keep him, but he is open to exploring other options.

Yaya Toure has hinted that he is open to leaving Manchester City this summer, citing a desire for new challenges and a feeling that he no longer belongs at the club. The 31-year-old midfielder has struggled to hit top form this season, and City are likely to try and sell him in the summer. Toure's former manager Roberto Mancini, now at Inter Milan, is reportedly interested in reuniting with the player. Toure has stated that he will not stay at City just for the money, and will consider a move if a new challenge is offered to him.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri for killing a man in a fit of rage over child support payments 16 years ago. Cole was convicted by an all-white jury and had several appeals denied by the US Supreme Court, including claims of mental illness and unfair jury selection. Cole's execution was carried out despite concerns from advocates that he was not mentally fit to die, and that the jury selection process was unfair. Cole was pronounced dead at 10:24pm on Tuesday, becoming the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year.

A Russian warship and two bombers strayed close to UK territory, prompting a response from the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force. The incident is believed to be an attempt by Russia to test Britain's defences, possibly in relation to a large NATO war games exercise taking place in Scotland. The Russian aircraft were intercepted by Typhoon fighter jets, and the warship was monitored by a frigate. The incident is the latest in a series of apparent tests by Russia, which has been increasing its military activity near the UK in recent months.

Curtis Stone, a celebrity chef, is adamant about feeding his two young sons, Hudson and Emerson, healthy food, and has never allowed them to eat hot dogs or other junk food. Stone believes that parents are responsible for shaping their children's eating habits and that kids will adopt whatever they are exposed to. He has dedicated his new cookbook, Good Food, Good Life, to his eldest son Hudson and features photos of himself cooking and gardening with his family. Manchester City players have expressed support for Patrick Vieira to replace under-fire manager Manuel Pellegrini if he is sacked at the end of the season. Vieira, a former Arsenal midfielder, is highly respected among the City players and has done well with the youth team and Elite Development Squad. The club's first-choice managerial option remains Pep Guardiola, who has made it clear he will stay with Bayern Munich for at least another season. If Guardiola is not available, Vieira is emerging as a strong contender to replace Pellegrini.

A herd of 15 buffalo escaped from a farm in Schodack, New York, and swam across the Hudson River, leading law enforcement to shoot and kill the animals after they ran down the Thruway, a toll road that connects major cities in the state. The buffalo were deemed too wild and untamable to be captured safely, and experts deemed tranquilizers ineffective. The farm's owner had admitted that capturing the animals unharmed was unlikely, and police used a helicopter to monitor the situation. The buffalo were eventually shot in a stream in Coeymans, about 10 miles south of Albany.

Wesley Sneijder, a Galatasaray striker, launched his knife range on the 15th anniversary of two Leeds United supporters being stabbed to death in Istanbul in 2000. He tweeted about the availability of his knife set, which was met with outrage from Leeds fans who were still grieving the loss of Kevin Speight and Christopher Loftus. Sneijder later deleted the tweet and apologized, saying he was unaware of the anniversary and had deleted the promotion. A minute's silence will be held before a match between Leeds and Blackburn Rovers to mark the anniversary.
